en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga,
Chapter on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at Kosambī in Ghosita’s Park.
Now at that time, a certain brahmin had prepared a milk-drink for the Saṅgha.
The bhikkhus were drinking the milk with a slurping sound.
A certain bhikkhu who had formerly been an actor said this:
“I think this entire Saṅgha has been cooled.
Those monks who were few in desires... [as before]... complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
“How can a monk act wantonly toward the Saṅgha?”... [as before]...
“Is it true, monk, that you committed an act of levity concerning the Saṅgha?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him... [as before]...
"How indeed, foolish man, can you act out of malice toward the Saṅgha?
This, foolish man, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
Having rebuked him... [and so forth]."
Having given a Dhamma talk, he addressed the monks:
“Monks, one should not treat the Buddha, the Dhamma, or the Saṅgha with levity.
Whoever should do so commits an offense of wrong-doing.”
Then the Blessed One, having rebuked that bhikkhu in many ways for being difficult to support...
[and so forth] ...and furthermore, bhikkhus, you should recite this training rule:
"The training is to be observed: 'I shall not eat making a *surusuru* sound.'"
One should not eat making a "suru-suru" sound.
Whoever, out of disrespect, eats making a "suru-suru" sound, commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense—
"Unintentionally... [and so on] ...for one who is a first-time offender.
The first training rule is concluded.
